subject: Approval request: Dedicated Burst Capacity private beta (2–3 customers) — rollout gates + risk summary
related_account: Design partner Dedicated accounts (2 confirmed, 1 pending)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 9:18 AM PT
Subject: Approval request: Dedicated Burst Capacity private beta (2–3 customers) — rollout gates + risk summary

Priya / Neha,

Requesting approval to run a private beta for Dedicated “Burst Capacity” with 2–3 design partner customers starting the week of 6/23 (exact date gated on readiness checks below).

Why now:
- We have repeated escalation patterns around predictable weekly/monthly spikes where customers either (a) overbuy baseline Dedicated capacity or (b) hit throttles and open support tickets. Recent example: SUP-3198.
- We now have a v1 design centered on strict admission control (no preemption guarantees), cooldown/backoff, and an explicit global circuit breaker.

What I’m asking you to approve:
1) Product approval to offer the burst beta under explicit pilot terms (best-effort burst, shadow metering, no SLA change).
2) Infra approval to allocate controlled burst pool headroom in 2 regions for pilot (details below), with hard “pause” conditions.

Proposed pilot customers (final selection in PM-641):
- 2 confirmed design partners in US/EU; 1 optional third if first two are clean.
- We will only enable burst behind a per-tenant feature flag + allowlist.

Proposed burst pool allocation (beta):
- us-east-1 (A100-80G): small shared burst pool sized for short-lived spikes (minutes) and capped per-tenant.
- eu-west-1 (A100-80G): same as above.

We are NOT promising:
- Any preemptive eviction ordering, cross-region arbitrage, or spot-market bursting.
- Any change to baseline Dedicated SLOs. Baseline stays isolated; burst is a separate “admitted or denied” path.

Rollout gates (must pass before we flip pilot tenants):
- Feature flag + per-tenant config validation in control plane
- Routing: baseline → burst pool → deny/fallback semantics implemented and tested
- SRE: dashboards + paging for burst saturation / reject rate / neighbor p99 drift; runbook complete
- Game-day: at least 1 simulated saturation + misconfig scenario with “disable burst” verified

Risk summary (high level):
- Capacity contention risk: burst pools could borrow too much from hosted headroom if mis-sized or if routing mistakenly spills.
- Noisy neighbor risk: within burst pools themselves; mitigated via hard caps, fairness, cooldowns.
- Customer confusion risk: deny semantics/retry guidance; mitigated via explicit docs + headers/reason codes.

Attachments:
- Burst_Beta_Approval_Request_-_Risk_and_Gates_v3.pdf
- Dedicated_Burst_PRD_v0.9.pdf
- Burst_Beta_Terms_-_Pilot_Addendum_v2.docx

If approved, I’ll send a short “go/no-go checklist” with DRI sign-offs (Fleet/SRE/Control Plane/Routing) and we’ll keep the pilot at 2 customers until metrics are stable for 2 weeks.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst Capacity private beta (2–3 customers) — rollout gates + risk summary

Thanks Lauren.

A few questions before I sign off:
1) Can we confirm the policy decision path is deterministic and cached safely? I want to avoid any “split-brain” behavior where two identical requests see different admission outcomes due to cache invalidation.
2) What’s the blast radius if a tenant config is wrong (e.g., limit fields unset)? Do we fail closed?
3) For auditability: are we logging “who changed burst settings” + “why was a request admitted/denied” in a way we can use during incident review?

If we can answer these cleanly and we’re failing closed by default, I’m supportive of a very small pilot.

— Priya



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 10:27 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst Capacity private beta (2–3 customers) — rollout gates + risk summary

Priya — agreed on all three.

Quick answers (and I’ll make sure these are explicit in the go/no-go checklist):
1) Determinism/caching: policy evaluation is deterministic on (tenant_id, region, pool_type, requested_concurrency, requested_tps) + config version. Cache key includes config version; cache TTL short; any config update bumps version and invalidates.
2) Fail closed: yes. Default is burst disabled. Any schema/validation failure means “not eligible” and we route baseline only (or deny if baseline saturated per existing behavior). No “implicit enable.”
3) Auditability: plan is to ship audit logs for config changes + policy decisions (admit/deny + reason code) in the same window as pilot readiness.

If you want, I can ask Jordan/Ethan to add a one-pager on the determinism/invalidation design, but net: we’re explicitly designing for “no surprises.”

Lauren



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 2:14 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst Capacity private beta (2–3 customers) — rollout gates + risk summary

I’m open to this with very explicit constraints.

Infra concerns are straightforward:
- Hosted commitments cannot be impacted. The burst pool must be isolated operationally (even if physically in the same cluster).
- I want a clear “pause the beta” policy: if we see sustained saturation, hosted p99 drift, or anything that looks like spillover, we stop.

Please confirm:
1) The initial pool sizes (GPU count / region) and what headroom we’re taking.
2) Hard per-tenant limits we’ll start with (concurrency, tokens/sec) and the cooldown defaults.
3) Who is on the hook to respond within 30 min if the burst pool goes sideways (paging policy).

If we can lock those, you have my approval to run with 2 customers first.

Neha



From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 3:01 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst Capacity private beta (2–3 customers) — rollout gates + risk summary

Jumping in for (1).

We can carve initial burst pools without taking from the baseline Dedicated reservations.
Proposal for beta (A100-80G):
- us-east-1: 16 GPUs in a dedicated “burst” node group with explicit labels (excluded from reservation allocator)
- eu-west-1: 8 GPUs same setup

Constraints / pause conditions:
- Burst pools are capped by an upper utilization gate; we can set an automated “no-admit” mode if hosted utilization exceeds threshold.
- Fleet will not auto-scale burst pools upward during beta without explicit approval.

If approved today/tomorrow, we can provision the node groups next week and keep them dark (no routing) until SRE signs off on dashboards + the disable procedure is tested.

Vanessa Ortiz
Fleet Engineering



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 4:12 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst Capacity private beta (2–3 customers) — rollout gates + risk summary

For (3) and the gating:

SRE will sign off only if the following exist before first customer traffic:
- Dashboards: per-tenant admit/deny rate, pool saturation, queueing, p99 latency for baseline vs burst, and “neighbor protection” indicators
- Alerts (paging):
  - burst pool saturation sustained > N minutes
  - burst deny rate spikes (indicative of contention or misconfig)
  - baseline Dedicated p99 drift correlated with burst activity (hard stop)
- Runbook: “disable burst for tenant” and “disable burst globally” are one-liners with validated permissions.

Paging ownership:
- During pilot: Primary page to SRE (oncall) + Fleet secondary if saturation indicates capacity issue.
- We need a named DRI for “business decision: do we keep burst enabled for tenant X?” (suggest Lauren/PM + Neha for infra guardrails).

If we see any signal of impact to hosted or baseline Dedicated, the default action is: disable burst globally first, investigate second.

Sean



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jun 5, 2025 at 5:03 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst Capacity private beta (2–3 customers) — rollout gates + risk summary

This is great — thank you.

Confirming the items Neha requested:
1) Pool sizes/headroom: aligned with Vanessa’s proposal (16 GPUs us-east-1, 8 GPUs eu-west-1), no reservation allocator exposure.
2) Starting limits (proposal for pilot; final defaults reviewed in design):
- Per-tenant hard cap: max concurrent requests and max tokens/sec (set conservatively; we’ll start low and ratchet)
- Cooldown/backoff: enabled by default; admission shuts off for a tenant for a short window after hitting cap; global circuit breaker triggers on sustained saturation
3) 30-min response: SRE oncall primary; Fleet secondary as needed; Product DRI (me) to decide tenant enable/disable within guardrails.

I’ll incorporate the explicit “pause policy” into the pilot plan and share a go/no-go checklist for sign-off early next week.

If you both reply with an explicit “approved for 2-customer pilot under these constraints,” I’ll proceed with scheduling the provisioning and customer comms.

Lauren



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 6, 2025 at 9:08 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst Capacity private beta (2–3 customers) — rollout gates + risk summary

Approved for a 2-customer pilot, with these conditions:
- Fail closed (burst disabled by default) and deterministic policy eval.
- Audit logging for config changes + admit/deny reason codes in place before first pilot traffic.
- Clear rollback: global disable takes effect immediately.

Please include those as explicit checklist items with owners.

Priya



From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jun 6, 2025 at 11:37 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst Capacity private beta (2–3 customers) — rollout gates + risk summary

Approved for 2-customer pilot under the constraints discussed.

Infra guardrails to be explicit in the runbook and checklist:
- No hosted impact: any sustained hosted p99 drift correlated with burst = immediate global disable.
- No scale-up of burst pools during beta without my approval.
- Pool admission gated on utilization thresholds (automated “no-admit” mode).

Keep me posted on the game-day date; I want someone from Infra leadership present for the first one.

Neha
